problem.title: Branched surfaces and triangulations — Question 7.1
problem.statement:
Characterize branched surfaces embedded in $3$–manifolds which can be
non–trivially split to a homeomorphic copy of themselves.
problem.background:
Calegari's author-source problem list contains 67 numbered questions on foliations and laminations of 3-manifolds.

problem.research_summary: Open as stated; no verified characterization. Literature status: Splitting of branched surfaces is a standard operation used throughout the theory of laminations and veering triangulations; it appears in Gabai–Oertel, and the split-complex/veering dictionary of Landes–Taylor and others uses branched-surface splittings. No explicit characterization of self-similarity under splitting was verified.

current_review_qualification.exact_gap: No legal embedded nontrivial splitting or compatible returned carrier is reconstructed from cone/operator data; no unrestricted reduction to pseudo-Anosov or atoroidal sutured depth-one veering hypotheses; no admissible prescribed-iterate complexes with a global unbounded-radius estimate; extension of the specified partial lamination L, if pursued, requires compatible preservation data beyond existence of some fully carried lamination.
